edges.effect_quant: The ovarian-cancer signal is one of the most consistent long-term benefits of combined oral contraceptives. Across pooled datasets, ever use is associated with lower risk, and longer duration generally strengthens that protection.
edges.population: premenopausal and postmenopausal women with prior exposure to combined oral contraceptives
edges.mechanism: Combined oral contraceptives suppress ovulation and reduce repeated epithelial disruption and inflammatory repair at the ovary. That cumulative ovulation-suppression model fits the duration-response pattern seen across cohort and pooled analyses.
edges.summary: Combined oral contraceptives are associated with lower ovarian-cancer risk in large pooled analyses, and the most persuasive evidence suggests the benefit grows with duration of use. This is one of the clearest long-term protective associations in reproductive cancer epidemiology.
edges.caveats: Most of the strongest evidence is observational, and formulations have changed across decades. The protective association also needs to be weighed against other outcomes, including small increases in some hormone-sensitive cancers.
